result.summary: R6’s unsupported diagnosis is fixed in S5. One product-risk claim still blocks closure: O1 incorrectly treats restart during a dream as losing only uncommitted work.

findings.title: O1 assumes a commit makes interrupted promotion atomic
findings.body: O1 says an interrupted run simply does not commit, so restarting cannot affect vault content. Actual promotion writes files individually before commitNamedSet runs (src/cli/dream.js:956,1055). src/core/dream/promote.js:1469-1495 publishes sequentially and explicitly documents partial publication without rollback at :810-812. A restart during that phase can therefore leave some vault changes published and others absent, with the transcript ledger still unadvanced (:1164). Restart after the commit but before ledger persistence can also leave committed work eligible for reprocessing. These are persistent partial-state/retry consequences, not merely the lost run O1 prices. The round-6 disposition repeats the unsupported assurance.
findings.recommendation: Remove the commit-based safety assurance from O1 and its round-6 logbook mirror. Explicitly price partial vault publication and interruption between commit and ledger persistence as restart risks; either accept those residuals or revise the recovery option. Do not imply transactional rollback.

next_steps: R6 closure check: reviewed every S5 sentence against acquisition, promotion and teardown. The vault-inactivity and impossible-recovery claims are withdrawn, restart names ongoing-work loss, and deletion remains conditional on checking for running dreams. S5, AC5 and AC7 use 'dream lock is overdue:'; the current spec contains no 'dream lock is stale:' literal.
